item.title: Trade Group to Strengthen Local Music Ecosystems in the U.S. Announces Launch
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest news and trends in the music industry. Today, we're talking about a new organization that's making waves in the world of music. Say hello to the Association of Music Offices, or AMO.
[Soft music continues in the background]
Host: The AMO is a national trade group that brings together municipal and state governments, community organizations, and industry partners to champion local music ecosystems. The organization was launched at the Music Biz conference in Atlanta, and it already has 14 founding members, including government music offices from cities like Dallas, New Orleans, and Nashville.
[Short music transition]
Host: So, what's the goal of the AMO? According to Matt Mandrella, the music officer for the city of Huntsville, Alabama, the organization aims to amplify the power of music ecosystems nationwide. Mandrella says that every city has a music scene, but most overlook it as an economic and quality of life driver. The AMO wants to change that by sharing expertise, fostering long-term economic impact, and promoting cultural vitality.
[Short music transition]
Host: The organization's initial focus will be on establishing governance and membership structures, developing data and measurement frameworks, and building community engagement models. They'll also create a central hub for resources, including toolkits, funding mechanisms, and education programs.
[Short music transition]
Host: Reid Wick, the Recording Academy's director of regional advocacy and member engagement, says that the AMO has the potential to transform how we support music at the state and local level. And with the organization's appeal for music offices and allied organizations to join, it's clear that the AMO is just getting started.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today's episode. If you're interested in learning more about the Association of Music Offices, you can visit their website at musicoffices.org. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you on the next episode!
